Oldham County sits just northeast of Louisville and is part of the I 71 corridor in north central Kentucky. The county clerk handles the annual sale of delinquent real estate tax claims, which Kentucky calls certificates of delinquency. This guide explains how Oldham County tax sales work, when they are usually held, how registration works, what investors can buy, and what steps matter most before you spend money.

What is Oldham County’s tax lien investing system?

Oldham County sells tax lien certificates, not tax deeds. In Kentucky, unpaid real estate taxes become certificates of delinquency after transfer to the county clerk. Third party buyers can register and buy those certificates at the county tax sale. The buyer earns statutory interest and may later enforce the lien under Kentucky law if the bill is not paid.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • Oldham County offers a tax lien certificate system, selling certificates of delinquency instead of tax deeds.
  • Tax sales typically occur in early August, with a 12% interest rate set by law for certificates.
  • Investors can participate by registering and submitting lists of bills, with a random drawing determining the order of sale.
  • The county’s proximity to Louisville supports housing demand, making it attractive for tax lien investors.
  • Due diligence is crucial; investors should verify property details and be aware of potential risks before bidding.

Fun Facts About the County

  • Oldham County was formed in 1824 and was Kentucky’s 74th county.
  • La Grange is known for freight trains running on Main Street.
  • Oldham County is part of the Louisville metro area and the I-71 economic corridor.

Attractions & Economic Highlights

  • Trains on Main in La Grange and the La Grange Railroad Museum are county standouts.
  • The Oldham County History Center adds local history and Underground Railroad stories.
  • I 71 is the main road link, with quick access to Louisville and Cincinnati.
  • Business services, manufacturing, health care, tourism, and farm-related activity all support the local economy.

Why This County is Ideal for Tax Lien Investors

  • Kentucky tax lien certificates offer high returns because state law sets interest at 12% simple per year.
  • Oldham County sits near Louisville, which helps support housing demand and resale interest.
  • The sale format is clear. Buyers submit lists, deposits, and pick in rounds after a drawing.
  • For many investors, that makes Kentucky tax lien certificates a solid low-risk investment compared with many other places where rules are less clear.

Auction Process for Tax Lien Sales

Oldham County uses the Kentucky certificate of delinquency system. This is not a bid down interest auction. The interest rate is set by law at 12% simple per year. Buyers do not compete by lowering that rate. Instead, registered buyers submit lists of bills they want. The county then runs a drawing to set order and sells certificates by rounds. Priority buyers with earlier year liens may claim matching current year bills before the regular lottery pool is assigned.

How the Auction Works

Here is a simple look at how the Oldham County tax lien auction works from registration through final payment.

  1. Complete the Required Registration

    Register with the Kentucky Department of Revenue if required for third party purchaser status. Then send the Oldham County registration form, affidavit, fee, and bill lists to the county clerk.

  2. Submit the Correct Type of Bill List

    If you already hold prior year liens on the same property, submit priority lists with full funds. If you want new purchases, submit lottery lists with a 25% deposit plus filing fees.

  3. Attend the Drawing in Person

    Show up for the drawing, since the clerk says all participants must be present. The drawing sets the order of sale.

  4. Select Certificates in Rounds

    Buyers select certificates in rounds. Oldham’s recent procedure used one bill each for the first five rounds, then three bills each after that.

  5. Pay the Full Balance by the Deadline

    Pay the full balance by the county deadline. Oldham’s recent procedure required full payment by 4:00 p.m. on sale day

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Oldham County Tax Lien Certificates

The headline return is 12% simple annual interest. That is the statutory rate on a Kentucky certificate of delinquency. Your actual yield depends on when the owner pays, what fees attach, and whether later legal work is needed. A quick payoff can still produce a solid annualized return. A long hold may earn more total interest, though collection costs and time matter. The best case is a clean redemption with no dispute. The harder cases may involve notices, legal fees, or foreclosure work after the one-year waiting period.

Open to All Investors / Foreign Investor Participation

Kentucky allows third-party purchasers to register and buy certificates of delinquency if they meet state requirements. The Department of Revenue handles that registration process. The Oldham County clerk also requires county sale forms, lists, deposits, and a notarized affidavit. The county materials do not limit the sale to local residents only. That means out of state and foreign investors can often take part if they complete the required state and county steps and can meet payment rules. Buyers should still confirm tax, entity, and legal issues with their own advisers before bidding.

Importance of Due Diligence in Oldham County Tax Lien Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check the exact parcel and owner record before you bid.
  • Review maps, access, use, and basic property conditions.
  • Check whether the bill is on your submitted list because you can only buy from that list.
  • Review mortgage, code, court, and title issues with a title search.
  • Confirm payoff amounts with official county data only.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • You may buy a lien on land with poor access or little resale value.
  • You may face extra legal costs before collection or foreclosure.
  • You may hold a certificate for a long time before payoff.
  • You may make bad return estimates if you ignore fees and timing.

Buying Over-the-Counter Liens in Oldham County

How to Purchase OTC Liens

Kentucky lets third-party purchasers buy prior-year certificates after they become available. The Department of Revenue notes that once a buyer is eligible, prior year certificates may be acquired at any time. Oldham’s procedures also state that unpaid bills not completed at the sale may later be available for purchase. Start with the county clerk’s delinquent taxes page and ask the clerk what remains open.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

OTC buying can mean less competition and more time to review each parcel. The interest rate stays set by statute. That can help investors who prefer a calmer process over sale day crowd pressure.

Why Oldham County is a Top Choice for Tax Lien Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Part of the Louisville metro area with I 71 access.
  • State set 12% interest gives clear return math.
  • County sale rules are posted online with forms and templates.

Real Estate Market Overview

Oldham County has grown in population and remains tied to the Louisville area. That usually supports owner occupancy, commuting demand, and long term housing interest. For lien buyers, that kind of setting can improve redemption odds because owners, lenders, and servicers often act to protect real estate in stronger markets. That does not remove risk, but it can help explain why Kentucky lien buyers often track counties near major job centers.

Conclusion

Oldham County is a Kentucky tax lien certificate county. It does not run a tax deed sale. The county’s recent materials show an early August sale, a 9:00 a.m. Eastern start, a La Grange courthouse area location, a required registration packet, and a drawing-based sale format. The interest rate is set by Kentucky law at 12% simple per year. That can make Oldham County a strong place to study if you want tax lien investing near a stable metro area. Still, smart investing starts with careful research, clear title work, and realistic expectations about time and legal costs.

Pro Tips

  • Focus first on parcels near stronger roads and built-up areas along the I-71 corridor.
  • Pull maps before the sale day so your submitted list reflects real parcel quality.
  • In Oldham County, rank your lottery list from best to worst because order matters.
  • Keep extra certified funds ready in case your picks run deeper than expected.
  • Track nearby Louisville area demand since that can affect redemption behavior.

FAQs for Oldham County Tax Liens

Do I get the property right away?

No. You buy a tax lien certificate, not the deed.

Can I renovate after the sale?

Not unless you later gain title through the legal process.

Do other liens disappear?

No. Always run title work before investing.

Can occupied property cause issues?

Yes. Possession and title are separate issues.

Can I finance resale plans with the certificate?

Some investors do, but lender rules vary a lot.
